ai system.Masquerading: Adversaries alter file names, locations, metadata, or appearances to deceive users and security tools into trusting malicious artifacts as legitimate or benign.
ai system.Cloud Service Discovery: Attackers leverage cloud provider APIs and tools to systematically identify enabled services, including AI models, security controls, and logging mechanisms across multi-service environments.
ai system.Corrupt AI Model: Corrupted model files can evade detection by scanners while still executing malicious code before deserialization fails.
ai system.LLM Response Rendering: Adversaries exploit client-side rendering of external images or embedded content to automatically exfiltrate private data via URL parameters.
ai system.Drive-by Compromise: LLM-based systems can be compromised by malicious content embedded in websites visited by users or retrieved by AI agents.
ai system.Stage Capabilities: Adversaries pre-position AI artifacts (poisoned datasets, malicious models, prompt injections) on controlled infrastructure or public platforms, often exploiting typosquatting or hallucinated entities to evade detection.
ai system.AI Agent Context Poisoning: Adversaries manipulate the LLM's context—such as memory or thread history—to persistently alter the agent's behavior.
ai system.AI Agent Context Poisoning: Memory: Adversaries can inject persistent malicious instructions or biases into an LLM's user-specific memory through prompt injection, enabling long-term manipulation across future sessions.
ai system.AI Agent Context Poisoning: Thread: Malicious instructions injected into a shared LLM thread can persistently alter the model's behavior across multiple users and sessions, with effects amplified by expanding context windows.
ai system.Modify AI Agent Configuration: Modifying AI agent configurations can persist malicious settings across sessions, alter system prompts, tools, or knowledge sources, and disable security controls to enable long-term covert actions.
ai system.RAG Credential Harvesting: Attackers exploit an LLM's access to retrieve credentials from a RAG database that has ingested internal documents.
ai system.Credentials from AI Agent Configuration: Attackers can compromise credentials stored in AI agent configuration files to gain direct, unauthorized access to external systems and services.
ai system.Discover AI Agent Configuration: Adversaries extract AI agent configurations via direct access or prompt-based probing to enable targeted exploitation.
ai system.Discover AI Agent Configuration: Embedde: Adversaries map an agent’s embedded knowledge to identify accessible data sources and sensitive content for targeted exploitation.
ai system.Discover AI Agent Configuration: Tool De: Adversaries exploit tool definitions to map the agent's capabilities, revealing accessible resources and potential attack vectors.
ai system.Discover AI Agent Configuration: Activat: Adversaries may probe for external-facing activation triggers to remotely initiate or hijack agent workflows.
ai system.Discover AI Agent Configuration: Call Ch: Adversaries may extract and exploit call chains in AI agent configurations that connect user inputs or LLM outputs to execution sinks, enabling targeted attacks via prompt injection.
ai system.Data from AI Services: Adversaries can exploit AI agents' extended tool and data access to collect sensitive information beyond normal user permissions.
ai system.Data from AI Services: RAG Databases: Retrieves stored data from an external knowledge base upon user prompts.
ai system.Data from AI Services: AI Agent Tools: Adversaries can exploit tool invocation to access and exfiltrate internal organizational data through connected APIs or services.
ai system.Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocatio: Adversaries exploit legitimate AI agent tools to encode and transmit sensitive data to attacker-controlled external destinations through seemingly routine operations.
ai system.Gather Victim Identity Information: Adversaries collect personal and sensitive identity details from various sources to enable convincing impersonation and targeted attacks.
ai system.Generate Deepfakes: Adversaries can rapidly scale impersonation and evade biometric systems by creating authentic synthetic media using reduced skill and effort.
ai system.Process Discovery: Adversaries enumerate running processes to identify AI-related software stacks, which can reveal credential access and lateral movement opportunities.
ai system.OS Credential Dumping: Attackers harvest stored authentication material like hashes, tokens, or plaintext credentials from system memory or caches to enable lateral movement and access to AI services and development tools.
ai system.Use Alternate Authentication Material: Attackers exploit pre-existing authentication artifacts like hashes, tickets, or tokens to impersonate users and bypass access controls without needing plaintext credentials.
ai system.Use Alternate Authentication Material: A: Tokens enable adversary access by bypassing standard authentication and directly authorizing API actions.
ai system.Manipulate User LLM Chat History: Adversaries can delete, edit, or restructure chat history to conceal malicious behavior and avoid user detection, especially when exploiting asynchronous history updates.
ai system.Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Ap: Adversaries inject persistent malicious prompts into public-facing input channels to be later ingested by AI systems, causing long-term downstream effects across multiple users and tools.
ai system.Delay Execution of LLM Instructions: Adversaries embed instructions contingent on a future trigger, such as a keyword or next interaction, to bypass turn-based security controls that restrict actions in the current context.
ai system.Search Open Websites/Domains: Adversaries gather victim information from public websites and domains, often using targeted search queries to identify specific platforms or services for subsequent exploitation.
ai system.Search Open Websites/Domains: Code Repos: Adversaries extract sensitive victim information, including AI system details, credentials, and employee data, from publicly accessible third-party code repositories.
ai system.AI Service API: This technique leverages AI service APIs to blend malicious commands with legitimate traffic, enabling stealthy, long-term command and control while reducing the adversary's footprint.
ai system.Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion: Adversaries dynamically alter their payloads or behaviors in response to detected artifacts of virtualized or analysis environments.
ai system.AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting: Attackers exploit AI agent tool access to extract credentials from integrated sources like document stores, code repositories, and productivity tools.
ai system.AI Agent Tool Data Poisoning: Adversaries inject malicious or misleading content into locations accessible to AI agent tools, often optimizing it for retrieval by common queries to trigger prompt injections or false outputs.
ai system.AI Agent Clickbait: Attackers embed deceptive prompts and visual cues in web content to trick AI agents into executing unintended actions, such as copying and running malicious code.
ai system.Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invoc: Adversaries can leverage an AI agent's tool-use capability to destruct data at scale, disrupting system and network availability.
ai system.Generate Malicious Commands: Adversaries dynamically generate varied malicious commands from natural language using LLMs, evading detection and enabling rapid tactical adaptation.
ai system.Deploy AI Agent: Adversaries deploy autonomous agents with excessive permissions and suppressed user oversight to execute predefined goals through tool and system interactions.
ai system.Publish Poisoned AI Agent Tool: Adversaries distribute poisoned tools via unregulated repositories or remote servers to inject malicious prompts that compromise AI agent behavior.
ai system.Escape to Host: Adversaries break isolation to access the host by disabling safety features or user confirmations in AI agent configurations.
ai system.Exploitation for Credential Access: Exploitation of software vulnerabilities allows adversaries to execute arbitrary code in order to steal credentials from compromised systems.
ai system.Exploitation for Defense Evasion: Exploitation of vulnerabilities in security software or system components to disable, bypass, or circumvent defensive measures.
ai system.AI Agent: Adversaries manipulate AI agents via prompt injection and configuration alterations to covertly execute commands and maintain persistent control for command and control operations.
ai system.AI Supply Chain Rug Pull: Adversaries initially publish legitimate AI components to gain user trust and adoption, then later replace them with malicious updates to bypass supply chain scrutiny.
ai system.AI Agent Tool Poisoning: Adversaries compromise benign tools to stealthily manipulate agent behavior, persist unnoticed, and execute malicious actions like data exfiltration or unauthorized commands.
ai system.AI Supply Chain Reputation Inflation: Adversaries use established, credible-looking trust signals—such as genuine developer accounts, adoption metrics, and benign releases—to disguise malicious updates that eventually compromise AI supply chain components.
ai system.Machine Compromise: Adversaries exploit or manipulate AI-enabled components to gain system access, enabling code execution, credential theft, data exfiltration, and persistence.
ai system.Machine Compromise: Local AI Agent: Adversaries can achieve full system compromise by hijacking local AI agents that have broad permissions to autonomously execute commands, access files, and control workflows.
ai system.Machine Compromise: AI Artifacts: Attackers can insert malware or malicious commands into AI models or datasets, which then execute through unsafe serialization or bundled scripts when accessed by other systems.
